name: NeRF/CuVol/NVol/SVox1

# NeRF/CuVol/NVol/SVox1

Also called: Volume Rendering (NeRF/CuVol/NVol/SVox1)

## Overview
This family implements [neural volume rendering](#1576-neural-volume-rendering.md) using sparse, hierarchical grid structures (specifically SVox2) to represent density and color fields, enabling efficient training and inference for novel view synthesis. It distinguishes itself from sibling methods like [Raymarching with 3D Volume Texture](10839-raymarching-with-3d-volume-texture.md) by utilizing learnable [sparse voxel grids](#8430-sparse-spatial-data-structures-for-nerf.md) with spherical harmonic basis functions for color, rather than fixed 3D textures, and from [Fixed-Point Volume Ray Casting](12056-fixed-point-volume-ray-casting.md) by relying on GPU-accelerated fused kernels for both forward and backward passes during gradient-based optimization.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family build on the core mechanism of [Direct volume ray casting](19-direct-volume-ray-casting.md) [G].

The implementation relies on a sparse grid structure (`SparseGridSpec`) that stores density (`density_data`) and spherical harmonic coefficients (`sh_data`) at active voxel locations. The rendering process is executed via fused CUDA kernels that handle [ray marching](#6739-ray-marching.md), alpha [compositing](#2436-compositing.md), and gradient computation in a single pass or tightly coupled sequence.

Key data structures include:
- `SparseGridSpec`: Contains `density_data`, `sh_data`, `links` (for sparse connectivity), `_offset`, `_scaling`, `basis_dim`, `basis_type`, `basis_data`, `background_links`, and `background_data`.
- `CameraSpec`: Defines camera parameters `c2w`, `fx`, `fy`, `cx`, `cy`, `width`, `height`, `ndc_coeffx`, `ndc_coeffy`.
- `RaysSpec`: Contains `origins` and `dirs` for the batch of rays.
- `RenderOptions`: Controls rendering behavior with `background_brightness`, `step_size`, `sigma_thresh`, `stop_thresh`, `near_clip`, `use_spheric_clip`, and `last_sample_opaque`.
- `GridOutputGrads`: Stores gradients `grad_density_out`, `grad_sh_out`, `grad_basis_out`, `grad_background_out`, `mask_out`, `mask_background_out`.

The forward pass computes the predicted RGB color by integrating along rays. If background links are defined and non-empty, a background color is accumulated. The transmission is computed in log space if [background rendering](#5042-background-rendering.md) is enabled or if a [beta loss](#1392-sparsity-and-beta-loss-regularization.md) is applied.

## Subtopics

### SVox2 Integration
The primary implementation uses the SVox2 library for sparse grid management. It supports dynamic upsampling of the grid resolution during training, adjusting density and weight thresholds to maintain sparsity. It also supports [background modeling](#12931-background-modeling.md) via separate background links and data. [Link](16745-specific-data-formats-and-integrators.md)

### Fused Kernel Execution
The rendering is performed using fused CUDA kernels (`render_ray_kernel`, `render_background_kernel`, `render_ray_backward_kernel`, `render_background_backward_kernel`) to minimize memory bandwidth bottlenecks. Thread block sizes are configurable via `TRACE_RAY_CUDA_THREADS`, `TRACE_RAY_BG_CUDA_THREADS`, and `TRACE_RAY_BKWD_CUDA_THREADS`. [S1, unofficial]

### Training Loop Integration
The method integrates with a standard PyTorch [training loop](#4290-training-loop.md), computing MSE loss between ground truth and predicted RGB, and updating grid parameters (density, [SH coefficients](#5603-spherical-harmonics.md), basis) with specific learning rate schedules. It supports sparsity and beta losses. [S1, unofficial]

## Background
The specific implementation details provided originate from the OSHMOS/IPRF project, an unofficial repository hosted on GitHub. The code demonstrates a practical application of neural volume rendering using sparse grids, focusing on efficient training and upsampling strategies. [S1, unofficial]
